diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The only failing test checks that Ystar_base values in Production!H60:H65 fall within 10,000-500,000 (thousands of millions of Georgian Lari). The baseline produced ~78 instead of ~78,000, indicating a units/scale mismatch: capital stock from PWT is in millions of 2017 US dollars while real GDP from WEO is in billions of Georgian Lari (or similar GEL units). The Cobb-Douglas formula EXP(lnZ)*K^alpha needs K and Y to be in consistent units, but the model mixed USD-denominated PWT capital with GEL-denominated WEO GDP, causing the output scale to collapse. The xlsx skill does not currently warn about unit consistency when combining data from multiple macroeconomic sources with different currencies/scales. This task-specific guidance should be added so the model either converts PWT capital to GEL (using exchange rate / PPP) or uses a consistent-unit capital series, ensuring Ystar values land in the millions-of-GEL thousands range.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill emphasizes zero formula errors and formatting conventions but gives no guidance on unit/currency consistency when combining data from multiple sources (PWT in millions of 2017 USD vs WEO GDP in GEL vs ECB CFC in GEL). The baseline passed all structural/formula tests but failed the magnitude test because K and Y were in incompatible units, producing Ystar_base ≈ 78 instead of ≈ 78,000. The skill should instruct that when building production-function or macro models mixing cross-source series, the agent must verify unit consistency (currency, scale: units/thousands/millions/billions, base year) across all inputs before computing combined quantities, and perform explicit conversions (e.g., apply a GEL/USD exchange-rate or PPP conversion to PWT rnna, or rescale WEO GDP) so that downstream outputs land in the expected magnitude. Add a sanity-check step: after computing a key output, compare it against the scale of the input GDP series to confirm order of magnitude agreement.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a new subsection under 'Requirements for Outputs' (or a new 'Multi-source data consistency' section) that states: (1) When combining economic/financial data from multiple sources (e.g., PWT, IMF WEO, ECB, national statistics), always verify and document the units, currency, and scale (units vs thousands vs millions vs billions) of each series in a header cell or comment. (2) Before using series together in formulas (production functions, ratios, accumulation equations), convert all series to a single consistent unit system — typically match the currency and scale of the target output. For example, PWT 'rnna' is in millions of 2017 US dollars while IMF WEO GDP for Georgia is in billions of Georgian Lari; apply an explicit FX/PPP conversion factor cell so K and Y share units. (3) After computing a headline output (e.g., potential GDP Ystar), perform an order-of-magnitude sanity check against the input GDP series — if Ystar differs from Y by more than ~10x, suspect a units mismatch and revisit conversions. (4) Prefer parameterizing conversion factors as named input cells (blue font) so they are visible and auditable rather than hidden inside formulas.
